chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Embassy visits and meeting local people
summary: Embassy engagements were catering to the head man, with monsoons in Ceylon and a sitar player, and little contact with locals.

blocks.x: When you were on the State Department
tours you were entertained at (unintelligible) entertaining the embassies and (unintelligible) of all the countries you visited, were you not?
Did you give concerts in the embassies?

Yes, we did some, and -- but, you see, mostly they catered to the head man. We were just there really. You get that feeling it's -- you're just invited because the head man was invited, so I didn't -- it was nice, but there wasn't too much activity, and it's strange -- everything was strange. And we had a couple of real good storms in the Middle East which were quite a revelation. And then we were down in the island of -- what's the island off the southern tip -- Ceylon. And that was something else, the storms and things, the rainstorms that they have down there -- sound like it's going to blow everything away. Call them
monsoons. We were in a couple of those.
In addition to being entertained at the American embassies, did you have much opportunity to meet people in the countries you visited?

Mostly you associated with the U.S.I.S. representatives and Americans that were over there in other capacities, not too many local people because they couldn't talk to you, number one, and so you stayed more or less to yourself, and then the trip was short, and there wasn't time to really get around.
Well, the concerts that you did, you did give concerts for the people, of these countries though.
Concerts, yes, uh-huh, they attended. Then apparently they appreciated them, and, you know, they went over fairly well with them. But they didn't understand too much.
Did you hear any music in the countries you visited played by the people of those countries?

At different spots -- we went to one embassy, and this world's greatest sitar player was there. He played a few numbers and things like that. And up in -- what are those two countries in the north of India? Pakistan -- I went to one of the meetings or one of the local Pakistani meetings of the -- what's this group -- Rotary Club thing and things like that, but it's only one day each place, so you
really didn't get a chance to see too much or hear too much.
